newsitem.title: USA: Circon board urges rejection of U.S. Surgical bid.
newsitem.headline: Circon board urges rejection of U.S. Surgical bid.

text.p: Circon Corp. said Monday its board of directors recommended that shareholders reject U.S. Surgical Corp.'s latest $218 million or $16.50 a share hostile buyout offer.
Circon, a maker of devices for minimally invasive surgery, issued a statement saying its board concluded that the offer, commenced Aug. 5, is "inadequate."
In July, U.S. Surgical announced its latest hostile tender offer to take full control of Circon, which it has been pursuing for a year.
U.S. Surgical, of Norwalk, Conn., already owns 14.8 percent of Circon. It makes products meant to lower the cost of surgery and other medical treatments.
U.S. Surgical's $16.50 per share bid is above its previous $14.50 per share offer but below its original $18 per share bid made over a year ago.

Last week U.S. Surgical said it reinstated a lawsuit against Circon, asking the company to provide information that would allow U.S. Surgical to communicate directly with Circon shareholders concerning its tender offer.
U.S. Surgical also said it sought a court order to force Circon to hold its 1997 annual meeting.
Circon last week said it scheduled a shareholders meeting for Oct. 6.
U.S. Surgical stock rose 31 cents to $32.75 on the New York Stock Exchange. Circon edged up 19 cents to $15.75 on Nasdaq.
